intervals.label: hosting the Mainz neutrino-mass experiment
intervals.note: No source consulted gives a founding date for the institute. The start is borrowed from the experiment's own earliest dated fact (first results in 1991); the interval is open because the same institute is listed on a 2025 ECHo paper. This is a lower bound for the experiment's hosting, not the institute's founding.
intervals.quote: Our spectrometer yielded first results in 1991

name: Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (Institute of Physics)
notes: Facility record for the host institute of the Mainz neutrino-mass experiment; the university itself is institution:johannes-gutenberg-university-mainz.

operator_text.quote: Institut für Physik der Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz, D-55099 Mainz, Germany

summary.plain: The Institute of Physics of Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz, Germany. In the 1990s and early 2000s it hosted a tritium beta-decay experiment that set one of the two best direct limits on the neutrino mass.
summary.technical: Institut für Physik, Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz: host of the Mainz tritium beta-decay neutrino-mass experiment (MAC-E filter, phases I-III) that preceded KATRIN.
